current_object.title: Outgoing source Helmholtz field: fundamental solution, Fraunhofer and Fresnel error terms
current_object.statement: For $k>0$ define $G_k(x)=e^{ik|x|}/(4\pi|x|)$ off the origin, a locally integrable complex function. Then $$(-\Delta-k^2)G_k=\delta_0$$ distributionally. For a finite complex measure $\alpha$ supported in $B_a(0)$, the field $u=G_k*\alpha$ is smooth outside the support, solves $(\Delta+k^2)u=0$ there and is outgoing: for $x=rn$, $r\ge2a$, $$u(rn)=\frac{e^{ikr}}{4\pi r}\int e^{-ikn\cdot y}\,d\alpha(y)+O\!\Bigl(\frac{\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}}{r}\Bigl[\frac{a}{r}+\frac{ka^2}{r}\Bigr]\Bigr)$$ uniformly in direction, and $r(\partial_ru-iku)=O(r^{-1})$ uniformly. For a planar aperture $y=(y_1,y_2,0)$ with observation $x=(\xi_1,\xi_2,z)$, $z>0$, $|\xi|\le b$, $a+b\ll z$, the Fresnel approximation replaces $R=|x-y|$ by $z+|\xi-y|^2/(2z)$ and $1/R$ by $1/z$ with phase error $O(k(a+b)^4/z^3)$ and relative amplitude error $O((a+b)^2/z^2)$, hence absolute field error $O(\|\alpha\|_{\mathrm{TV}}z^{-1}[(a+b)^2/z^2+k(a+b)^4/z^3])$. Aperture data are an explicitly specified scalar source, not asserted to be the unknown exact Maxwell boundary traces, and no uniqueness or existence for arbitrary obstacle boundary data is claimed.
current_object.strategy: For radial $f(r)$ one has $\Delta f=f''+2f'/r$ by direct coordinate differentiation of $\partial_ir=x_i/r$ ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]), and inserting $f=G_k$ gives $(\Delta+k^2)f=0$ for $r>0$. For the distributional identity excise a ball $B_\delta$ inside a compact test integration; the second Green identity ([[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) on the excised domain cancels the $k^2$ terms and leaves the inner flux, where $G_k=1/(4\pi\delta)+O(1)$ and $\partial_rG_k=-1/(4\pi\delta^2)+O(1)$: the derivative-test boundary term is $O(\delta)$ and the leading unit flux multiplies $\psi(0)$, while the local $k^2G_k$ integral is $O(\delta^2)$; the limit is $\delta_0$ with the displayed sign. Off-support smoothness and all derivatives follow from the positive separation of compact observation and source sets, with differentiation under the source integral. For the Fraunhofer error write $R=|rn-y|$ and use the norm expansion of the cited dipole-remainder technique ([[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]]): $|R-r+n\cdot y|\le Ca^2/r$ and $|r/R-1|\le Ca/r$; the exponential difference is bounded by $C r^{-1}(a/r+ka^2/r)$ via $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$, and integrating against the total variation of $\alpha$ with the integral triangle inequality ([[thm-integral-triangle-inequality]]) gives the displayed error; the outgoing relation follows from $\partial_rR=1+O(a^2/r^2)$ and $R^{-2}=O(r^{-2})$. The Fresnel estimate is the Taylor expansion of the norm with explicit remainder on the compact small-$s$ region $s=|\xi-y|^2/z^2$, using $|e^{i\theta}-1|\le|\theta|$.

current_object.title: Outgoing spherical radial functions: exact bounds on the spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient
current_object.statement: For $l\in\mathbb N_0$ and $z>0$ set $$h_l(z)=(-i)^{l+1}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\sum_{j=0}^{l}\frac{i^j\,(l+j)!}{j!\,(l-j)!\,(2z)^j}.$$ Then $h_l$ is a complex-valued $C^2$ function of $z>0$ solving $$h_l''(z)+\frac2z h_l'(z)+\Bigl[1-\frac{l(l+1)}{z^2}\Bigr]h_l(z)=0,$$ it never vanishes on $(0,\infty)$, and its Wronskian-type identity $\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_l(z)}\,h_l'(z)\bigr)=z^{-2}$ holds. For $k>0$ and $R>0$ the spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient $$t_l=\frac{k\,h_l'(kR)}{h_l(kR)}$$ satisfies the exact bounds $$\operatorname{Re}t_l\le-\frac1R,\qquad |\operatorname{Re}t_l|\le\frac{l+1}{R},\qquad 0<\operatorname{Im}t_l\le k .$$ These are exact identities and inequalities for the displayed explicit functions, not asymptotic formulas; the argument uses only elementary differentiation and a constant Wronskian, so no large-$l$ asymptotic input is required.
current_object.strategy: Substituting $h=e^{iz}P(z)/z$ with $P(z)=\sum_{j=0}^l b_jz^{-j}$ into the radial equation gives the coefficient recursion $b_{j+1}=i(l+j+1)(l-j)b_j/[2(j+1)]$ with $b_0=1$, terminating at $j=l$ because $l-j=0$; its solution is the displayed factorial formula, which proves the equation and shows the leading outgoing term $(-i)^{l+1}e^{iz}/z$ with a finite remainder. Writing $y=zh_l$ gives $y''+(1-l(l+1)z^{-2})y=0$ with real coefficient; differentiating $\operatorname{Im}(\overline y\,y')$ and using the equation shows its derivative is zero, so by the zero-derivative-implies-constant corollary on the interval $(0,\infty)$ ([[cor-zero-derivative-implies-constant]]) it is constant, and its large-$z$ leading exponential gives the constant $1$: hence $\operatorname{Im}(\overline{h_l}h_l')=z^{-2}\ne0$, so $h_l$ never vanishes. For the real bounds set $F=|y|^2=|P|^2$; since $b_j$ carries phase $i^j$ times a real number, odd cross terms cancel and $F$ is an even finite polynomial in $z^{-1}$, $F=\sum_{j\ge0}a_jz^{-2j}$ with $a_0=1$. Differentiating the real equation gives $F'''+4(1-l(l+1)z^{-2})F'+4l(l+1)Fz^{-3}=0$, whose coefficient matching yields $a_{j+1}=(2j+1)[l(l+1)-j(j+1)]a_j/[2(j+1)]$, all positive for $0\le j\le l$ and zero at $j=l+1$, with the closed form $a_j=(2j)!(l+j)!/[2^{2j}(j!)^2(l-j)!]$. Thus $|h_l|^2=z^{-2}\sum a_jz^{-2j}\ge z^{-2}$ and half the logarithmic derivative gives $\operatorname{Re}[kh_l'/h_l]=-R^{-1}\bigl[\sum_ja_j(kR)^{-2j}+\sum_j j a_j(kR)^{-2j}\bigr]/\sum_ja_j(kR)^{-2j}$, a weighted average of $j\in\{0,\dots,l\}$, so it lies in $[-\,(l+1)/R,\,-1/R]$. The Wronskian identity gives $\operatorname{Im}[kh_l'(kR)/h_l(kR)]=k/(k^2R^2\,|h_l(kR)|^2)=k/(k^2R^2|h_l|^2)\in(0,k]$ using $|h_l|^2\ge z^{-2}$. The derivative computations use the algebra of derivatives and the entireness of the complex exponential ([[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]], [[thm-complex-exponential-is-entire-with-derivative-itself]]).

current_object.title: Spherical harmonics: orthogonal decomposition, complete basis and addition theorem
current_object.statement: Let $P_l$ denote the real vector space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$ on $\mathbb R^3$, $H_l=\ker(\Delta:P_l\to P_{l-2})$ with $P_k=\{0\}$ for $k<0$, and let spherical harmonics of degree $l$ be the restrictions of $H_l$ to $S^2$, with unnormalised surface measure $d\Omega$ of total mass $4\pi$. Then $P_l=H_l\oplus|x|^2P_{l-2}$, $\dim H_l=2l+1$, harmonics of distinct degree are orthogonal in $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$, and the union over $l$ of the spaces of spherical harmonics admits a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For any real orthonormal basis $Y_{lm}$, $m=1,\dots,2l+1$, of degree-$l$ harmonics the addition theorem holds: $$\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}Y_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n')=\frac{2l+1}{4\pi}P_l(n\cdot n'),$$ where $P_l$ is the Legendre polynomial of the convergent zonal kernel lemma ([[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]). The Laplacian is the Euclidean one ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). This supplies the harmonic decomposition, orthogonality, completeness and exact addition kernel; it does not assert higher boundary regularity.
current_object.strategy: For homogeneous $Q$ of degree $l-2j$, Euler's identity $x\cdot\nabla Q=(l-2j)Q$ gives $\Delta(r^{2j}Q)=2j(2l-2j+1)r^{2j-2}Q+r^{2j}\Delta Q$; the ansatz $H=\sum_ja_jr^{2j}\Delta^jP$ with $a_0=1$ and $a_j=-a_{j-1}/[2j(2l-2j+1)]$ cancels consecutive coefficients in $\Delta H$, and the final $\Delta^{\lfloor l/2\rfloor+1}P$ vanishes by degree, so $H$ is harmonic and $P-H$ is divisible by $r^2$; recursion gives the decomposition. For homogeneous harmonic $H_l,H_m$ the Green identity on the ball ([[cor-second-green-identity-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]) gives $0=\int_{S^2}(H_l\partial_nH_m-H_m\partial_nH_l)=(m-l)\int_{S^2}H_lH_m$, whence orthogonality of distinct degrees; if a harmonic of degree $l$ equalled $r^2Q$, its orthogonality to all lower-degree harmonics would force $\int_{S^2}H_l^2=0$, so $H_l=0$; the monomial count $\dim P_l=(l+1)(l+2)/2$ gives $\dim H_l=2l+1$, and restriction is injective by the same homogeneity argument. For density, continuous functions are dense in $L^2(S^2)$ by a finite smooth graph atlas with subordinate smooth cutoffs, pulling each localised function back, mollifying and using the $L^2$ translation and approximate-identity interfaces ([[lem-complex-translation-and-approximate-identity-interfaces]]); the restricted real polynomial algebra is unital and separates points, so Stone-Weierstrass ([[thm-real-stone-weierstrass-general]]) makes it uniformly dense in $C(S^2)$, and the homogeneous-degree decomposition puts every restriction in the finite span of spherical harmonics, giving $L^2$ density. Finite Gram-Schmidt ([[thm-gram-schmidt-orthonormalisation]]) applied to a fixed ordered monomial elimination basis of each $H_l$ produces the orthonormal bases without an undefined basis selection. For the addition theorem, $K_l(n,n')=\sum_mY_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n')$ is independent of the orthonormal basis and rotation-invariant, and for fixed $n'$ it is the unique (up to scale) rotation-invariant homogeneous harmonic polynomial of degree $l$, which is the coefficient $|y|^lP_l(n'\cdot y/|y|)$ of the convergent kernel of the zonal lemma ([[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]); evaluating the diagonal by integrating $K_l(n,n)$ gives $(2l+1)/(4\pi)$, completing the addition theorem.
